title: Instrument attention-window timeline and kernel-choice scoring for prefill/decode hotspots
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Add fine-grained instrumentation around attention-window lifecycles and the kernel selection scoring path so we can attribute latency/cost regressions to specific attention shapes and scheduler decisions. This ticket covers: (1) NVTX range conventions for attention forward/backward and KV cache interactions, (2) emitting a per-request kernel_choice_score and chosen_kernel_id as trace/span attributes, (3) timeline bucketing for long-context prefill operations to reveal scheduling stalls, and (4) a dashboard and SLI probe to detect kernel-selection oscillation during traffic bursts.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime emits NVTX ranges for: attention.prepare_window, attention.apply_mask, attention.forward_heads, kv.cache_load, kv.cache_store and scheduler.select_kernel with consistent naming and stable start/end timestamps.
Each inference request trace contains kernel_choice_score (float) and chosen_kernel_id (string) as span tags for both prefill and decode phases.
Grafana dashboard shows kernel_choice_score distribution and kernel-switch frequency per 5m window; baseline comparison panel to previous 7 days.
Automated end-to-end test that asserts kernel-choice attributes present for synthetic long-context (>4k tokens) requests in CI smoke run.
No regressions in p50 latency for short-context (<=512) workloads in canary cluster; documented rollout plan if regressions observed.
tasks: Define NVTX naming convention and field set in telemetry spec (telemetry/ATTN-TIMELINE-2025.md)
Implement NVTX RAII helpers in runtime core and wrap attention inner loops
Emit kernel_choice_score and chosen_kernel_id in tracer span creation path for scheduler.select_kernel
Add lightweight sample counter to scheduler to detect oscillation for same request across retries
Extend telemetry exporter to map kernel_choice_score to metric series 'kernel.choice.score' and chosen_kernel_id to tag 'kernel_id'
Create Grafana panels and alert (kernel-switch-rate > threshold) in observability project
Add CI smoke test and unit tests for span attribute presence and NVTX tags
comments: 2025-11-18 - Aisha Patel: Initial writeup. Motivation: recent customer report that long-context pipelines intermittently pick an expensive kernel which spikes p99. We need attribution to decide whether scheduler or kernel fingerprinting is at fault.

2025-11-19 - Marco Li: Implementing NVTX helpers. PR draft opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7891. Initial microbench shows no measurable overhead in short trace runs (~0.2% wall time).

2025-11-20 - Priya Menon (PM): Please add a panel that correlates kernel_choice_score with memory residency (GPU mem pct) — that helps determine if selection is memory-driven. Also flag customer impact thresholds.
2025-11-21 - Marco Li: Updated PR to include chosen_kernel_id as span tag and added kernel_choice_score normalizer (0..1). Running dogfood runs on dedicated-dev cluster (dedicated-dev-3).

2025-11-22 - Eng Reliability (review): Reviewed NVTX naming; suggested switching to dot-separated scope names (runtime.attention.forward) to align with tracing conventions. Also requested that NVTX ranges include kernel fingerprint id in metadata when available.

2025-11-23 - Aisha Patel: Added rollout plan: (a) land instrumentation behind feature flag runtime.telemetry.attn_timeline, (b) enable in dedicated-dev for 48h, (c) evaluate kernel-switch-rate and p99 deltas, (d) enable read-only exporter for hosted telemetry team, (e) full rollout to canary if no regressions. If p99 increases >5% for short-context, rollback.
